import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
EMB = 16
HID = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.n_types = spec.n_types
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        T = spec.n_types
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, T * EMB, 1)
        self.mix = nn.Conv2d(T * 3 * EMB, T * HID, 1, groups=T)
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(T * HID, T, 1, groups=T)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        e = self.cell(f)
        B, _, Y, X = e.shape
        e = e.reshape(B, self.n_types, EMB, Y, X)
        parts = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            et = e[:, t]
            mx = F.max_pool2d(et, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-et, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(et, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            p = torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            p = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            parts.append(p)
        h = torch.cat(parts, dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.mix(h))
        place = self.out(h).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.film = nn.Linear(WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.mix = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f2 = F.relu(self.mix(f) + self.film(g)[:, :, None, None])
        place = self.place_head(f2).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 16
GW = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.in3 = nn.Conv3d(5, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.in2 = nn.Conv2d(3, WIDTH, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, zc], dim=1)
        flat = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        h = F.relu(self.in3(x) + self.in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        place = self.place_head(h)
        place = torch.logsumexp(place, dim=2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.in3 = nn.Conv3d(5, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)

        self.cell = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, T * EMB, 1)
        self.mix = nn.Conv3d(T * 3 * EMB, T * HID, 1, groups=T)
        self.out = nn.Conv3d(T * HID, T, 1, groups=T)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

            av = F.avg_pool3d(et, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)

        hp = torch.cat(parts, dim=1)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 16
GW = 64


class Net(nn.Module):

        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.in3 = nn.Conv3d(5, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.in2 = nn.Conv2d(3, WIDTH, 1)
        self.colmix = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH * spec.Z, WIDTH * spec.Z, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, zc], dim=1)
        flat = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        h = F.relu(self.in3(x) + self.in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))

        h = h + m.reshape(B, WIDTH, Z, Y, X)

        place = self.place_head(h)
        place = torch.logsumexp(place, dim=2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 16
GW = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.in3 = nn.Conv3d(5, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.in2 = nn.Conv2d(3, WIDTH, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, 2, (3, dy, dx)) for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, zc], dim=1)
        flat = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        h = F.relu(self.in3(x) + self.in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        qs, gs = [], []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            p = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1, 1, 1))
            o = self.heads[t](p)
            qs.append(o[:, 0])
            gs.append(o[:, 1])
        q = torch.stack(qs, dim=1)
        w = torch.softmax(torch.stack(gs, dim=1), dim=2)
        place = (w * q).sum(2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.v_c2 = nn.Conv3d(CW, CW, 3, padding=1)

        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)

        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        q = self.place_head(h)

        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        v = F.relu(self.v_in3(x) + self.v_in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))
        v = F.relu(self.v_c2(v))
        vg = self.v_glob(torch.cat([v.mean((2, 3, 4)), v.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))

        flat = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        h = F.relu(self.in3(x) + self.in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        hx = torch.cat([h, x], dim=1)
        qs, gs = [], []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            p = F.pad(hx, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1, 1, 1))
            o = self.heads[t](p)
            qs.append(o[:, 0])
            gs.append(o[:, 1])
        q = torch.stack(qs, dim=1)
        w = torch.softmax(torch.stack(gs, dim=1), dim=2)
        place = (w * q).sum(2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: r3c1 + nonlinear footprint head
trials.hypothesis: Change: each per-type footprint conv (3, dy, dx) now outputs 8 hidden channels, followed by a ReLU and a grouped 1x1 conv to the score and the gate. Why: 'every covered cell is right and nothing gets sealed' is an AND across cells, which one linear map expresses poorly. A hidden layer can learn this min-like test, the effect r1c1's min-pool showed in 2D. The cost is about 1.3x. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.85.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 16
GW = 64
HH = 8


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.T = spec.n_types
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.in3 = nn.Conv3d(5, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.in2 = nn.Conv2d(3, WIDTH, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, HH, (3, dy, dx)) for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.hout = nn.Conv3d(self.T * HH, 2 * self.T, 1, groups=self.T)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, zc], dim=1)
        flat = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        h = F.relu(self.in3(x) + self.in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        hs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            p = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1, 1, 1))
            hs.append(self.heads[t](p))
        hh = F.relu(torch.cat(hs, dim=1))
        o = self.hout(hh).reshape(B, self.T, 2, Z, Y, X)
        q = o[:, :, 0]
        w = torch.softmax(o[:, :, 1], dim=2)
        place = (w * q).sum(2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: r3c1 + taller 5-layer footprint head
trials.hypothesis: Change: the per-type footprint head kernel becomes (5, dy, dx), padded 2 layers in z, so it reads layers z-2 through z+2 instead of z-1 through z+1. Why: a brick lands where everything above its footprint is clear, and cells it seals can sit more than one layer away, so the gate and score need more of the column. Unlike r3c2's extra layer, this costs only about 1.06x. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.85.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 16
GW = 64
KZ = 5


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        self.in3 = nn.Conv3d(5, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.in2 = nn.Conv2d(3, WIDTH, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv3d(WIDTH, 2, (KZ, dy, dx)) for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, zc], dim=1)
        flat = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        h = F.relu(self.in3(x) + self.in2(flat).unsqueeze(2))
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        pz = KZ // 2
        qs, gs = [], []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            p = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1, pz, pz))
            o = self.heads[t](p)
            qs.append(o[:, 0])
            gs.append(o[:, 1])
        q = torch.stack(qs, dim=1)
        w = torch.softmax(torch.stack(gs, dim=1), dim=2)
        place = (w * q).sum(2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3, 4)), h.amax((2, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: No trials yet. The only evidence is the baseline's 4 seeds (0.541, 0.160, 0.160, 0.518). Seeds either succeed or fail, so a 2-seed mean can move by about ±0.15 from luck alone, and only large gains will be meaningful. The baseline sees a 5x5 patch around each cell and scores each brick from a 1x1 head at its anchor cell. It has no explicit link between a brick and all the cells it covers, no global context in the placement scores, and no structure shared across height layers. Whether a brick fits exactly depends on every covered cell at the landing layer, so heads that pool over the footprint, and encoders that treat height (z) as a spatial axis, are likely to help. Round 1 tests two cheap refinements (a footprint-pooled head and global context fed into the placement head) and one new idea (a layer-aware 3D convolution encoder), all kept at roughly 1 to 1.3x the baseline's compute.
analyses.2: The layer-aware 3D encoder (r1c3) did best with a mean of 0.557, but its two seeds scored 0.889 and 0.225, so a lot of that mean is seed luck. Still, it is small (0.91x the starting compute) and its strong seed is far above anything else. Footprint pooling (r1c1, 0.406) gave a modest gain and more even seeds. Feeding a FiLM-style global vector into placement (r1c2, 0.204) hurt, so avoid global modulation for now. Two weaknesses stand out in r1c3. First, its score readout uses logsumexp over z, which does not pick out the layer where a brick actually lands. Second, two 3x3x3 convs see only about 2 layers up and down, but the landing layer depends on the whole column. This round builds on r1c3 with one change each: a learned z-attention readout, footprint pooling in 3D, and a layer that mixes each whole column.
analyses.3: Treating the board as a 3D voxel grid is the clearest win so far. r1c3 scored 0.557 and r2c1 scored 0.691, against 0.345 for the starting architecture. Both are cheap (0.92x compute) and get the full 131k steps. Seed luck still matters most. The best seeds reach about 0.88 in every 3D trial, but weaker seeds drop to 0.16–0.51, so raising the mean mostly means preventing those failed seeds. Using a learned gate to pick the landing layer (r2c1) beat logsumexp. Some ideas hurt: max/min/mean footprint pooling plus an MLP in 3D was slower and got fewer steps (0.514), and a dense mix over each whole column broke weight sharing across layers (0.294). Adding a global vector in 2D (r1c2) also hurt. This round tests three single changes to r2c1: (1) a linear placement head that reads exactly the brick's footprint plus the layers just below and above it; (2) a third, residual 3D conv layer, so each cell sees more of its column; (3) a separate small critic, to see whether value-loss interference causes the failed seeds.
analyses.4: Two changes made the big gains. First, a 3D voxel encoder with weights shared across layers (r1c3, 0.557). Second, readouts that match the physics: a softmax gate over z that picks the landing layer (r2c1, 0.691), then a per-type head whose kernel covers the brick's exact footprint over 3 layers (r3c1, 0.906, both seeds high). r3c1 is the first model that did not collapse on any seed. Ideas that cost more compute, and so got fewer training steps, all failed: a third conv layer at 1.67x, footprint pooling at 1.31x, and a separate critic. Generic extra capacity also failed: dense column mixing and FiLM. So structure aligned with the task helps, and lost training steps hurt. In this last round I make three cheap changes to r3c1's footprint head: (A) feed the raw voxels to the head as a skip input, so it reads the exact missing and extra cells under the brick; (B) add a small nonlinear layer to the head, so it can express 'every covered cell is right'; (C) make the head kernel 5 layers deep instead of 3, so it sees more of the column.
